summary:
EXPLOG is a dynamic platform that finds locations on Earth with environmental conditions similar to planned permanent base sites on the Moon and Mars. Comparing data from many different sources with Earth regions is slow and complex, so EXPLOG brings everything into one system.

The user selects a region on Mars or the Moon by entering coordinates. EXPLOG collects data from planetary archives and Earth data sources such as NASA, USGS, Copernicus, ESA, and JAXA, organizes it in a JSON structure, and maps the variables. A Random Forest-based AI model then evaluates the data and returns potential analog regions on Earth with a comparison. Parameters include temperature, elevation, slope and topography, water and drought conditions, solar radiation, and soil and surface properties.

Static data was first used to validate reference points. The system is now built for dynamic data flow and easy addition of new sources, planets, and regions.

Its innovation is combining Earth, Moon, and Mars data in one research environment. Future goals include broader data coverage, better comparison methods, more planets and regions, and more accurate, reliable results.
details: EXPLOG is an AI platform that matches Moon and Mars base sites to similar Earth locations. It gathers NASA and Earth data, structures it in JSON, and uses Random Forest analysis to rank analog sites, helping researchers prepare for missions.
